title: Police board pleads for patience as fatal shooting investigation continues
article: The Norfolk Police Services Board is pleading for patience as the investigation into the Nov. 3 shooting death of Rodger Kotanko continues.

"We just ask citizens of Norfolk and our public to be very patient and have faith in our system," George Santos, acting chair of the police services board, said Wednesday. "I truly have faith in the Special Investigations Unit.
"We are well aware of what has happened but our citizens clearly have to understand that we cannot comment."
The board can't do anything that would jeopardize the investigation, he added.
"We just have to be very patient and to wait and see what the outcome is," Santos said. "I understand an investigation can take up to three months and could take longer."
Santos made the comments at the end of Wednesday's police services board meeting. He told the board he has responded to 136 calls since the fatal shooting.
Santos said the calls have come from people from all walks of life both in and outside of Norfolk. But the response has always been the same - the board can't comment.
Santos also sent condolences to the Kotanko family on behalf of the police services board.
Kotanko died after being shot four times inside the gunsmith shop next to his house on Port Ryerse Road, west of Port Dover, during a search by members of the Toronto Police Service.
Few details of the interaction have emerged since the province's Special Investigations Unit (SIU) launched a probe into the fatal shooting.
The SIU is an arm's-length body that investigates deaths, serious injuries and allegations of sexual assault that occur during the course of policing.
Kotanko, 70, was known to be a skilled gunsmith.
Family members and citizens have been looking for answers. Just over a week ago, the Kotanko family appealed to an unknown "customer" who was in the shop at the time of the shooting to come forward.
Three weeks ago, Haldimand-Norfolk MPP Toby Barrett said his office had received numerous e-mails and telephone calls from local residents looking for answers.
Barrett also extended condolences to the Kotanko family.
But, as a public office-holder, Barrett said he has been told to avoid commenting on the shooting pending the outcome of the investigation.
